2_Introduction: The target device achieved a champion PCE of 16.6912% (VOC: 1.0359 V, JSC: 22.664 mA/cm², FF: 71.0935%).The target PSCs achieved an average power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.6912% with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 22.664 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.0359 V and a fill factor (FF) of 71.0935%. In formulating the active solution, Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L was utilized to establish the perovskite layer. The perovskite was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s and finally at 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL chlorobenzene as antisolvent was dropped 6 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ at 1.73 mol/L, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—where the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation, MA⁺ tunes lattice strain and accelerates crystallization kinetics, and the dominant FA⁺ provides optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) for α-phase stabilization and reduced halide vacancy formation—while the partial Br⁻ substitution (10%) widens the bandgap marginally to improve VOC without inducing excessive lattice distortion or phase segregation; the precisely controlled two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) enabling uniform precursor wetting and nucleation site distribution, followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) inducing rapid solvent expulsion and shear-aligned crystal growth—combined with antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered 6 s before spin termination) to arrest intermediate solvated phases (e.g., PbI₂·DMSO or FAI–PbI₂ adducts) at an optimal supersaturation threshold, thereby promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing random grain boundary proliferation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete ligand ejection, facilitates Ostwald ripening for enlarged grain sizes (>500 nm), relieves residual tensile stress evidenced by narrowed XRD (110) peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ reflections at ~12.6°, and enables full conversion to phase-pure, highly oriented α-perovskite with minimized trap-state density at grain interiors and boundaries—collectively yielding high carrier diffusion lengths (>1.2 µm), suppressed non-radiative recombination, and enhanced charge extraction efficiency; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the ternary-cation composition synergizes with the kinetic control of crystallization to passivate undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites *in situ*, while the Br⁻ incorporation further stabilizes the lattice against ion migration and moisture ingress, as corroborated by uniform film coverage and high grayscale intensity across optical micrographs, homogeneously distributed PL intensity with >3× enhancement and monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ ≈ 380 ns) indicating low spatial heterogeneity in non-radiative pathways, and XRD patterns showing sharp, symmetric (110) and (220) reflections without peak splitting or broadening—mechanistically confirming minimal microstrain, high crystallinity, and suppressed defect clustering that jointly underpin the high VOC of 1.0359 V, JSC of 22.664 mA/cm², FF of 71.0935%, and champion PCE of 16.6912%.
